context.canonical_title: JVM 常见垃圾回收算法

required_checks: Verify the candidate directly answers both restored source rows asking JVM garbage-collection algorithms and does not drift into a collector-only answer.

Verify textbook reclamation mechanisms are clearly separated from concrete HotSpot collectors so mark-sweep, evacuation/copying, compaction, generational organization, parallelism and concurrency are not falsely presented as one-to-one collector identities.

Verify current-version claims are bounded to Oracle JDK 25, including the supported collector set and the server-class default-selection boundary rather than stating G1 as an unconditional JVM default.
Verify Eden and two Survivor spaces are explicitly scoped to the Serial collector implementation example and are not generalized to every HotSpot collector.

Verify G1 is described as region-based, generational, mostly concurrent and evacuating, with stop-the-world evacuation pauses and concurrent work, rather than reduced to a single textbook algorithm label.
Verify collector selection and tuning are evidence-driven and discuss pause/latency, throughput, live set, allocation rate, heap, CPU and footprint tradeoffs without fabricated production metrics.

Verify Full GC troubleshooting does not claim a single universal cause; distinguish evacuation failure, concurrent-cycle progress, humongous-object pressure, explicit GC and other contextual causes where applicable.

Verify the concept-answer contract includes a concise definition, shared comparison dimensions, selection conditions, inapplicable boundaries, concrete confusions/counterexamples and at least three topic-specific answered follow-ups.
review_contract.promotion_boundary: Do not promote or fabricate human approval. This canonical is in the pilot review scope and requires the repository's mandatory human-review attestation after evidence and deterministic audit pass.

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Introduction to Garbage Collection Tuning
claims_to_check: HotSpot provides multiple collectors for different requirements and collector selection can require workload-specific tuning
HotSpot uses generational scavenging and aging, parallel or concurrent work, and compaction as implementation techniques

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Garbage Collector Implementation
claims_to_check: generational collection relies on the weak generational hypothesis and young collections are strongly affected by the live-object set
the Serial collector example uses Eden plus two Survivor spaces and copies survivors between spaces before aging into old
throughput, latency, footprint and promptness impose competing tuning goals

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Available Collectors
claims_to_check: the current documented collector choices include Serial, Parallel, G1 and ZGC
Serial is single-threaded, Parallel is throughput-oriented and generational, G1 is mostly concurrent and balances pauses with throughput, and ZGC is low-latency oriented

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Ergonomics
claims_to_check: server-class machines default to G1 while Serial is the fallback default outside that boundary
maximum pause-time and throughput goals compete and heap sizing also affects footprint and pause behavior

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Garbage-First (G1) Garbage Collector
claims_to_check: G1 is generational, incremental, parallel, mostly concurrent, stop-the-world and evacuating
G1 uses regions and performs incremental space reclamation with stop-the-world pauses while long whole-heap work can run concurrently

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Garbage-First Garbage Collector Tuning
claims_to_check: G1 tuning should start from defaults and diagnostics rather than indiscriminately applying old tuning options
Full GC and long-pause diagnosis can involve evacuation failure, humongous-object pressure and other specific causes rather than one universal explanation
